about: A spear: a leaf-shaped iron head on a long wooden shaft. Today a hunting spear swung as a tool; later held in one hand with a shield or in two.

hands.source: holding.md section 1 (a spear among Two's examples) and its count: spear.single, spear.shielded and spear.two

open.why: today it is held and swung in the main hand alone, as a tool: the two-handed IK and the spear's second grip are not built (attachment.md Second grip, a listed fault)

lead.source: D463 and holding.md's lead: Main for every two-hander but a bow; the left on a left-handed body

grip_type.source: D562: in hand, a power grip closed by touch on the shaft; the off hand's too, on the second grip

slots.name: head
slots.joins: its socket (socket.mouth and socket.bottom on the shaft's line); the shaft made to their diameters, its top at socket.bottom

slots.name: shaft
slots.joins: a round shaft along +Y from its butt

slots.name: binding
slots.joins: its bore on the shaft: over the socket's mouth (its rivets' band) or at the grip

slots.name: butt
slots.joins: its bore over the shaft's -Y end (a butt spike)

grip.how: on the shaft at the reference's share of its length from the butt (0.75 of 1.8 m, 42%; D546's polearm 30 to 55%), near the balance: the item's origin

second.how: a point on the shaft a fixed distance from the grip (negative, toward the butt), part of the reference item, not of the envelope (research/2026-10-28-assembled-items-animation.md section 3), at least 4 cm from the butt (attachment.md Second grip)

open.why: its distance is set with the spear's two-handed takes, keyed with both hands; none exist

edge.how: the head's tip point and its two edges (edge.lower to the tip, ±Z) carried through; the hit is a thrust along +Y first

held.how: in the main hand's socket today, with no ready pose

open.why: its guards come with spear.single, spear.shielded and spear.two; D461 orders the two-handed stance next (its example a greatsword)

used.how: as a tool today: a blow plays the walker's Sword_Attack (terra_walker::figure); items.ron's tool.strikes, the hardest and furthest

open.why: its thrusts and sweeps come with its sets, two-handed ones keyed with both hands

carried.how: upright at the side in the main hand, point up (D567): the forearm forward, the shaft within 5 degrees of upright, held in the body's frame (attachment.md Carried)

stowed.how: a polearm across the back (D567, D551), beside a shield there

open.why: the turn and offset on the socket are not set (attachment.md Stowed's next step); a 1.8 m spear across the back must clear the head and the ground

blocking.how: two-handed: blocks with the weapon (holding.md's Two stance); with a shield, the shield blocks

open.why: no two-handed block clip; it comes with spear.two

animation.how: none yet: no spear set; as a tool it plays the walker's clips

open.why: spear.single, spear.shielded and spear.two (holding.md's count), in D461's order

length_m.source: art/held/spear.json length; the look's bounds measured 1.800

mass_kg.source: the head and a 0.03 m ash shaft 1.8 m long (670 kg/m^3, recalled), 0.85 kg; a stand-in until its parts are weighed. The look's shaft is 4.0 cm across (research parts-art section 4), thicker than a real one

balance_m.source: computed from the head at 1.7 m and the shaft's middle, from the grip at 0.75 m

inertia_kgm2.source: D459's I = m (b^2 + L^2/12) on the numbers above

grip_diameter_m.source: a real spear shaft about 3 cm across (recalled)

inertia_kgm2.source: D459's tempo clamp 0.85 to 1.15: I_ref/1.15^2 to I_ref/0.85^2

head_mass_kg.source: the inertia band at the reference's length, solved for the head (-56% to +76%: the shaft carries most of the inertia)

balance_m.source: the inertia band at the reference's mass and length, solved for the balance

envelope.state: computed from stand-in masses; no spear clips; for two hands the second grip stays the reference's across the envelope (research section 3)
